name: Tabo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Schlatter, Tim 2003. Tabo language grammar sketch (Aramia River). SIL PNG, 354pp
earlier_scan.note: Large SIL grammar sketch exists; sil.org blocked (not reachable by automated download), not on archive.org/OLAC mirror

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2021. The phonetics of Papuan languages in Southern New Guinea: an overview. In Lindsey & Schokkin (eds), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C SP 24), 5-12. hdl 10125/24999
sources.note: No Tabo/Waia mention. p. 7 generalises over the six languages in that volume only ('no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama'); not a statement about Tabo.
sources.venue: Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C SP 24)

sources.note: Phonology section gives only the phoneme inventory, cited to Evans 2018; no stress statement. References: Evans 2018, Schlatter 2003, TransNewGuinea.org.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2012. Even more diverse than we had thought: the multiplicity of Trans-Fly languages. In Evans & Klamer (eds), Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia (LD&C Special Publication 5), 109-149. hdl 10125/4562
sources.note: Does not mention Tabo or Waia at all (0 hits); nothing on Tabo stress.
sources.venue: Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia (LD&C Special Publication 5)

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area (Pacific Linguistics D-90). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Bibliography only. Its Waia index line lists Reesink 1976 and Wurm & Hattori 1981; older items are Papua Annual Report 1919-20 / 1920-21 100-word vocabularies of the Hiwi tribe and of Hibaradai, Mawadai and Eriga villages. No phonology work listed for Waia up to 1996.

sources.citation: Genesis in the Tabo Language of the Western Province of Papua New Guinea (Aramia River Dialect). 1993. Port Moresby: Bible Society of PNG. Rosetta Project scan, 8 pp. (archive.org rosettaproject_knv_gen-1)
sources.note: Scripture text only (orthography shows a: for a vowel, presumably ae); no linguistic notes, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Reesink, Ger P. 1976. Languages of the Aramia River area. In Reesink, Fleischmann, Turpeinen & Lincoln (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 19 (Pacific Linguistics A-45), 1-37. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A45.1
sources.note: Section 7 Waia (book pp. 21-25); 7.3 'Notes on phonology' (p. 25) gives only a tentative phoneme list (p t k b d g m n h l w y; i e a o u, possibly open-mid e/o; long vowels 'quite frequent and seemed to be phonemic'; no clusters except Cw/Cy) and says more data is required for morphology/grammar. Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the paper (a full-text search for stress/accent: 0 relevant hits).
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 19 (Pacific Linguistics A-45)

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. (ed.). 1973. The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea (Pacific Linguistics C-26), Waia notes pp. 14-17 and wordlist p. 592.
sources.note: The earliest professional record of Waia; may carry phonetic transcription with stress marks in the wordlist even if no rule is stated. Open on the PL archive but sealang.net refused connections.
Coded from Schlatter 2003 by R. E. Herrera Miranda; Grambank has no stress features, so nothing usable.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas et al. 2018. The languages of Southern New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide, 641-774. De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Regional survey chapter that contains a Tabo phoneme inventory (cited by Wikipedia); its phonology section may note prosody per language, and it is the only published (non-manuscript) modern description that treats Tabo.
sources.venue: The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide

sources.citation: Schlatter, Tim. 2003. Tabo language grammar sketch (Aramia River). Ms., 354 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only substantial grammar of the language (Glottolog doctype grammar, Grambank's sole source); a 354-page SIL sketch almost certainly opens with a phonology chapter that states stress placement. Glottolog source key silpng:silpng2001-2003:104 shows it is catalogued in the SIL PNG archive.

sources.citation: Territory of Papua. 1921. Vocabulary of the Hiwi tribe, Western Division; Vocabulary of the villages named Hibaradai, Mawadai and Eriga. Papua Annual Report for 1919-20, pp. 122-123.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Oldest Waia/Tabo wordlists (Carrington 1996 entries); colonial-era 100-word lists, so a stress statement is very unlikely; listed only for completeness of the bibliography.

sources.citation: Schlatter, Tim (and/or Sandra Schlatter). n.d. Tabo phonology essentials / organised phonology data / orthography paper, SIL PNG (existence unverified).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL PNG teams normally file a phonology essentials or OPD alongside a grammar sketch; the 1993 Genesis and 2006 Tabo (Fly River) NT imply an orthography statement exists. Not found in Glottolog, so it may be archive-only. Check the OLAC/SIL listing for knv when those hosts are reachable.

sources.citation: Hein, Veronika. 2000/2001. The role of the speaker in the verbal system of the Tibetan dialect of Tabo/Spiti. LTBA 24(1), 35-48.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Glottolog attaches these two records to tabo1241 by name-match error: they describe the Tibetic dialect of Tabo village, Spiti (Himachal Pradesh, India), not this PNG language. Irrelevant.

sources.citation: OLAC 'Resources in and about the Tabo language' (http://www.language-archives.org/language/knv)
sources.note: Both OLAC hosts (language-archives.org, olac.ldc.upenn.edu) refused connections; the Internet Archive copies exist (2010-2025) but web.archive. Would show whether SIL PNG holds a Tabo phonology/orthography paper besides the grammar sketch.
